section: Perspectives in Education · Ch4 — Teaching Methods (Complete)
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: A teacher divides the class into small mixed-ability groups, assigns each group member a specific role, and structures the task so that the group's success depends on every member contributing and helping one another, rather than working individually or competing. This teaching strategy is called:
explanation: Cooperative learning structures group work around positive interdependence and individual accountability, so members must collaborate for the group to succeed — distinct from mere group seating without structured interdependence.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch4 — Teaching Methods (Complete)
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: Before starting a lesson on 'uses of water', a teacher asks students to rapidly call out as many ideas as possible without any idea being criticised or evaluated at that stage, later organising and discussing the ideas generated. This technique is called:
explanation: Brainstorming generates a large quantity of ideas quickly by deferring judgement/criticism until later, encouraging free thinking and participation — commonly used to activate prior knowledge before a lesson.
